blocks.note: an eye is the organ that looks
a firework or balloon going off is popping

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a stunning beauty is losing their looks.

explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes your eyes bulge out in surprise is amazing, so the compound adjective is a vivid synonym.

clue.text: All in plate, very thin gruel

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spread across their boundaries

blocks.note: read straight through, ignoring spaces and the comma, from the last letter of the first word to the first of the last

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the whole serving on their plate was watery porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run spans four words, starting with the final E of 'plate' and ending on the G of 'gruel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean the whole lot, every single thing without exception, so they are straightforward synonyms.

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take the end letter of each word

blocks.note: the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what, in the end, is the thing that gets scrambled.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the last letters spell the answer, and the clue as a whole describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrambled eggs are the classic breakfast dish, so the item you scramble is naturally this breakfast food.

blocks.note: first meaning: first
second meaning: a chance

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words seem to describe a first chance; they are two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning first or introductory, and a noun meaning a chance or vacancy that has appeared.

blocks.note: first meaning: fairly or rather
second meaning: attractive or pleasing to look at

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite appealing' reads as a mild compliment; it is two meanings of one word, an adverb and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means fairly or moderately, and as an adjective it means attractive in a delicate way.

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the following words is used, a run lifted from inside them

blocks.note: read across the word breaks: the end of the first word, all of the second, most of the third

explanation.surface: A chip served alongside a pork chop, in part of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles three words, taking the N of 'on', the A, and the first four letters of 'chop'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a single tortilla chip, the Mexican snack usually served with melted cheese and toppings.

clue.text: Punished as a teenager, Don urged to reform

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: the name and verb taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A boy called Don, punished as a teen, is told to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks Don to reform his behaviour; it is his name and the verb that get rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents ground a misbehaving teenager by forbidding them from going out, a common household sanction.

indicators.note: the lead is the front, so losing it drops the opening letter

blocks.note: a beagle is a breed of hunting dog

explanation.surface: A bird dog, used in hunting, slips free of its leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird dog' looks like one phrase for a gundog, and 'lead' like a leash; split them, and lead means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey, so it is a simple example of the general class.

clue.text: Heart shown by men, but not head, in second performance

indicators.note: a head is the top or first part, so without it the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
the core is the heart or centre of something

explanation.surface: Male performers show real heart, if not brains, when called back on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shown by' places the heart word beside the shortened men; the clipped word comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is an extra piece performed after the main show at the audience's demand, a repeat appearance on stage.

blocks.note: first meaning: dull and uninspired
second meaning: a person travelling on foot

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a boring hiker; it is one word that serves as both adjective and noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means dull or lacking flair, and as a noun it names someone going on foot.

the letter to be forgotten

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 4 down, PRETTY, in its sense of 'fairly'

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 4 down is PRETTY, used here in its adverb sense, as in pretty good.

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' looks like the person doing the cutting; it is a verb telling you to alter the two words that follow.

clue.text: Respect paid by a gentleman originally welcomed into house

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of a word, its first letter
a guest welcomed into a place ends up inside it, so one part goes within another

blocks.note: a home is a house
taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Respect paid' sounds like the whole definition, but 'paid by' only joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is honour or reverence shown publicly to someone, so it is a close synonym of respect.

blocks.note: first meaning: to span or cross, as a road does over a river

explanation.walkthrough: Minors is the legal term for children; said aloud it matches the word for coal workers.

blocks.note: novel means new or original
a sprint is a short fast race

explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book; it is the adjective meaning fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the cheap, rough paper newspapers are printed on, so it is a specific kind of paper.

explanation.walkthrough: To pip, in British usage, is to beat by a whisker, as in pipped at the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper plays the bagpipes or another pipe, so the word names a kind of musician.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Small enough' reads as one phrase; split it into the size abbreviation and a word for sufficient.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a small quantity taken for testing or showing, the same as a test sample.
